page.layout: One column of text. Above it a running head and page number. Four stanzas of Latin verse, then a decorative headpiece, a centred title in capitals with a subtitle, and a paragraph opening with a woodcut initial. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Talem vir placido pectore diligit Consortem thalami: moribus & colit Insignem placitis: ornat & illius Virtutes variis laudibus inclytas.
Inter fœmineos fulgidior micat Cœtus, queis pietas: sanctaq; castitas, Queis seruata suis coniugibus fides, Et queis grata domus cura placet sua.
Vultus conspicui forma breuis perit: Siccis rara genis gratia defluit: Cunctis clara viget tempore fœmina Quæ puro Superum corde timet Patrem.
Talem fama vehat lucida, & urbium Magnis egregiam cœtibus indicet, Vt virtus meritis nobilibus nitens Laudem, & digna ferat præmia gloriæ.
main_text.head: DE PROVIDENTIA DEI RERVM OMNIVM Gubernatrice.
main_text.p: ODi prophanos. Hinc procul impiæ Gentes,Olympo quæ superum negant Regnare Numen: quaq; cæcas

page.notes: The woodcut initial O is joined to the first word "Di" as "ODi". The headpiece ornament above the title is not text and is not transcribed. Faint show-through text in the right margin is left out. The catchword "Cuncta" is set with a ct ligature in print and is given here as plain letters. The first stanza's "pectore" and similar ct forms are transcribed as plain letters.
